data.name: Juniper
data.gender_notes: Juniper is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word juniperus, meaning 'young tree'. In ancient Rome, juniper berries were considered precious and symbolized eternal life. In the Bible, the burning bush was believed to have been a juniper tree. The name Juniper carries the meaning “Young tree, precious stone” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Juniper usually hope their child will grow to embody young tree, precious stone and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Juniper belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Young tree, precious stone.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Juniper total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Juniper holds cultural significance in several aspects for Christians. Juniper berries were once used as a substitute for holy communion during times when the Eucharist was unavailable. Furthermore, the name Juniper has been popular among English Christians for centuries, and according to one source, there were 353 people named Juniper in England in 1600.
data.spiritual_significance: In spiritual terms, the juniper tree symbolizes purity, protection, and renewal. The name Juniper can be considered a reminder to cultivate a pure heart before God, to seek His protection, and to look forward to spiritual renewal. Additionally, the name Juniper can be seen as a connection to the Burning Bush event in Exodus, a symbol of God's presence and grace.
